# How dispatch retires the worker and tree of a finished ticket

## Overview

dispatch does not retire a ticket's worker the moment the ticket finishes. Each `tick` (dispatch.go:`tick`, run on an interval by dispatch.go:`run`) works out which treehouse leases belong to tickets that have left the started statuses. It reads the git state of those trees and plans a `Teardown`, `Keep` or `Stop` action for each one. These actions are planned first, so a tree freed by a teardown can be used by a launch in the same tick. A Teardown closes the herdr workspace, checks the tree again, deletes untracked files with `git clean -f -d`, and gives the tree back with `treehouse return <path> --if-lease-holder <id> --force`.

Planning is pure (`reconcile.Plan`, which has no side effects). All I/O happens in dispatch.go before planning (reading herdr, treehouse, Linear and git) and after it (the executor switch in `tick`). That is why `--dry-run` prints exactly the actions a real tick would take.

## Key Concepts

- **Lease holder.** treehouse records the ticket identifier as the `LeaseHolder` of each tree it leases (internal/treehouse/treehouse.go:`Tree`). A lease is the only link from a finished ticket to its leftover resources.
- **Finished / paused.** These come from config `[linear.statuses]`: `done` defaults to Done, Canceled, Duplicate, and `paused` defaults to Backlog, Todo (internal/config/config.go). dispatch never moves a built ticket to Done itself. Linear's GitHub integration does that when the PR merges (docs/guide.md:38).
- **Worker.** A herdr *workspace* whose checkout path equals the tree path, plus the `claude` agent inside it (internal/worker/worker.go:`onTree`). Retirement closes the whole workspace (`herdr workspace close <id>`). It never closes an individual tab or pane.
- **Unfinished.** Tracked work that returning the tree would destroy: modified or staged tracked files, or commits reachable from HEAD that no remote has (internal/treehouse/treehouse.go:`Unfinished`). Untracked files never count as work.
- **TeardownWarned.** A cache flag that makes sure a kept dirty tree gets exactly one Linear comment (internal/cache/cache.go).

## How It Works

```
tick (dispatch.go)
 ├─ herdr.Read ─────────────► snapshot (workspaces, tabs, agents)
 ├─ treehouse.Status per repo ► trees (path, LeaseHolder, RepoDir)
 ├─ lin.ManagedTickets ───────► started tickets (In Progress/Review/Needs Human)
 ├─ leaseHolders ─────────────► lin.LeasedTickets for holders NOT in managed
 ├─ leaseWorkers ─────────────► worker.FindAll per holder (one per tree)
 ├─ inspectTrees ─────────────► Unfinished / CheckErrors / Untracked per tree
 │                               (only for in.Retires(t) tickets)
 ├─ reconcile.Plan ───────────► retire() actions first, then parents, watch, launches
 ├─ settle(cache, ..., held=heldFinished)
 └─ executor switch:
      Teardown → teardown()   Keep → keep()   Stop → stop()
```

### 1. Finding finished tickets
`ManagedTickets` returns only started tickets, so a ticket that finished simply stops appearing in it. dispatch.go:`tick` collects every tree from `treehouse.Status` across all configured repos. retire.go:`leaseHolders` then picks out the lease holders that are not in the managed set and asks Linear for them with `LeasedTickets` (internal/linear/linear.go). That query returns the tickets whatever their status, archived ones included, but only those assigned to the key owner that carry the `ai` label, plus any whose labels were cut short. If every lease belongs to a managed ticket, the Linear call is skipped. If the lookup fails, only teardown is skipped this tick. Launches and nudges still run.

retire.go:`leaseWorkers` maps each holder to one `worker.Worker` per tree it holds (`worker.FindAll`). A ticket can hold several trees, one per repo. On each worker, `WorkspaceID` is set whenever any workspace shows that tree. `State` is not `None` only if a `claude` agent is in that workspace.

### 2. Reading git state before planning
retire.go:`inspectTrees` runs only for tickets where `Input.Retires` is true (status in Done and not a design ticket). For each tree it calls `treehouse.Unfinished`, which runs `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` and `git rev-list --count HEAD --not --remotes`. It also calls `treehouse.Untracked`, which runs `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z`. A tree whose git state can't be read goes into `CheckErrors`. All git calls use `gitEnv()`, which strips `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` and similar variables and sets `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`. That way a dispatcher started from a git hook can't point `git clean` at the wrong repo, and the checks can't collide with the worker's own git commands.

### 3. Planning (internal/reconcile/retire.go)
`Plan` begins with `actions := append(in.retire(), in.planParents()...)`, so retirement goes first. `retire()` handles each lease holder:
- If the status is neither Done nor Paused, the holder is ignored. This covers In Review and Needs Human holders.
- If `LabelsTruncated` is set, the result is `Skip`, because dispatch can't rule out a design ticket.
- Tickets labelled `design` or `design-review` are dropped silently. Their trees belong to the grill and review skills.
- A paused ticket gets a `Stop` for each tree that has a live Claude worker. The tree stays leased.
- A finished ticket goes to `retireFinished`, which decides each tree separately:
  - CheckError, or not inspected: `Skip`, and the tree stays leased.
  - Clean and pushed: `Teardown` carrying `RepoDir`, `WorkspaceID`, `TreePath` and the `Untracked` list. The reason is "clean and pushed" or "would remove untracked …".
  - Unfinished: `Keep`. Its `WorkspaceID` is set only if a Claude agent is live there. All Keeps for one ticket share a single comment, carried on the first Keep, and only if `Cache[id].TeardownWarned` is false. A Keep with no live worker and no comment to post is dropped.

### 4. Executing (dispatch.go executor + retire.go)
retire.go:`teardown` runs these steps in order:
1. `herdr.CloseWorkspace(WorkspaceID)`, if a workspace exists. It closes even an agentless workspace, because a worker whose Claude exited leaves one behind.
2. **Re-check** with `treehouse.Unfinished`. The worker may have written to the tree after the plan was made, or while it was being killed. If work turns up now, it prints a `keep` line and returns without commenting. The next tick's plan sees the dirty tree and posts the comment (teardown_test.go:`TestTickKeepsTheTreeOfWorkWrittenWhileTheWorkspaceClosed`).
3. `treehouse.Untracked` again. If files are present, it runs `treehouse.RemoveUntracked` (`git clean -f -d`, which leaves ignored files alone) and lists the untracked files again. If anything survives, it prints `keep … survived git clean` and does not return the tree. The usual survivor is a nested git repo, which `git clean` skips without `-ff`. Otherwise the reason becomes "removed untracked …", so the log names what was actually deleted rather than what the plan predicted.
4. `treehouse.Return(bin, RepoDir, path, holder)`, which runs `treehouse return <path> --if-lease-holder <id> --force`. The holder pin means a tree re-leased to someone else since the snapshot is left alone.

retire.go:`keep` closes the workspace (only when a live worker's ID was set) and posts the comment. It sets `TeardownWarned` only after Linear accepts the comment, so a refused comment is retried next tick. retire.go:`stop` just closes the workspace.

Errors from all three are printed to stderr, not returned, so one bad tree doesn't block the rest.

### 5. Cache bookkeeping
dispatch.go:`settle` handles tickets that no longer appear in the managed read. It keeps `TeardownWarned` only while retire.go:`heldFinished` says the ticket still holds a lease, so the flag disappears once the tree is returned. If the lease lookup failed or any pool was unreadable, `held` is nil and every warning is kept, so the comment is not reposted (tests at teardown_test.go:570 and :591). A ticket that comes back into the managed set with a changed status has `TeardownWarned` reset. A reopened ticket that finishes dirty again therefore gets a fresh comment (teardown_test.go:951).

## Where Things Live

- dispatch.go:`tick`: gathers the inputs, calls Plan, calls `settle`, and runs the executor switch (lines ~209–516). `settle` is at ~534.
- retire.go: `leaseHolders`, `inspectTrees`, `heldFinished`, `teardown`, `stop`, `keep`, `leaseWorkers`.
- internal/reconcile/retire.go: `Retires`, `notDesign`, `retire`, `retireFinished`, `NameList`.
- internal/reconcile/reconcile.go: the `Teardown`/`Stop`/`Keep` kinds, the `Action` and `Input` fields, and the `Plan` ordering.
- internal/treehouse/treehouse.go: `Status`, `Return`, `Unfinished`, `Untracked`, `RemoveUntracked`, `gitEnv`.
- internal/herdr/herdr.go: `Read`, `CloseWorkspace`.
- internal/worker/worker.go: `FindAll` / `onTree`, which map a tree to a workspace and agent.
- internal/linear/linear.go: `ManagedTickets`, `LeasedTickets`.
- teardown_test.go: about 45 end-to-end tick tests covering each branch. docs/guide.md, section "Teardown and pausing", gives the user-facing description.

## Gotchas

- **Two kinds of "keep".** The plan-side `Keep` comments on Linear. The `keep` lines printed inside `teardown` (late work, or files surviving `git clean`) are only log lines. For late tracked work, the next tick's plan posts the comment. For a nested repo that survives `git clean`, there appears to be no path that ever comments. Each tick re-plans a Teardown (untracked files never keep a tree in the plan), runs `git clean` again, and prints the same `keep` line, with no comment and no escalation. This is a reading of the code, and no test was found that runs more than one tick in this case.
- **Partial teardown.** Untracked files are deleted before `treehouse return`. If the return then fails (for example, treehouse refuses it), the files are gone but the tree stays leased. It is retried next tick.
- **Close-workspace failure** aborts the teardown before any git work runs, so the tree stays leased (`TestTickKeepsTheTreeWhenTheWorkspaceWillNotClose`).
- **Asymmetric workspace closing.** Teardown closes any workspace on the tree. Keep and Stop close one only if a Claude agent is in it, so a workspace opened by hand on a kept or paused tree stays open.
- **"Pushed" is strict.** HEAD must be reachable from some remote-tracking ref. A branch squash-merged and then pruned from the remote counts as unpushed, and its tree is kept until it is discarded by hand. Other local branches are ignored, because treehouse returns a tree by detaching HEAD.
- **Scope limits.** Tickets not assigned to the key owner, or without the `ai` label, are never torn down. Neither are design tickets, or tickets with truncated labels (those get a `Skip` line). Holders in In Review or Needs Human are not lease holders in this sense, since they are still managed.
- **Gaps.** `herdr.Read`'s full parsing, the internals of the `treehouse return --force` binary, and the `dispatch run` loop beyond its interval wiring were not read.

# How dispatch retires a finished ticket's worker and tree

## Overview

Retirement is part of the dispatcher's normal tick, and it follows the same plan-then-execute split as everything else. The tick starts from the trees, not the tickets. It finds every treehouse worktree whose lease holder is not among the managed (started) tickets, fetches those tickets from Linear, and checks the git state of the trees that may be retired. The pure planner `reconcile.Plan` then emits one of `Teardown`, `Keep`, `Stop` or `Skip` for each tree. Finally `dispatch.go` runs those actions. A `Teardown` closes the herdr workspace (the worker), checks the tree again, deletes untracked files with `git clean -f -d`, and hands the tree back with `treehouse return --if-lease-holder <id> --force`.

The design is careful about losing work. A tree is returned only if it has no tracked changes and every commit reachable from HEAD exists on a remote. Otherwise the worker is stopped, the tree stays leased, and Linear gets one comment explaining why. Retire actions come first in the plan, so a tree freed in this tick can be used by a launch in the same tick.

## Key Concepts

- **Lease holder**: `treehouse.Tree.LeaseHolder` is the ticket identifier that leased the tree (`internal/treehouse/treehouse.go`). A finished ticket is found because it still holds a lease, not because it shows up in the managed-ticket query.
- **Done / Paused statuses**: set in config. Defaults are `Done = {"Done","Canceled","Duplicate"}` and `Paused = {"Backlog","Todo"}` (`internal/config/config.go:75-76`). A Done ticket gets retired. A Paused ticket only has its worker stopped and keeps its tree.
- **Worker**: a herdr workspace whose `CheckoutPath` equals the tree path, plus the `claude` agent pane inside it (`worker.onTree` in `internal/worker/worker.go`). Closing the workspace retires the worker.
- **Unfinished vs Untracked**: deliberately separate checks.
  - `treehouse.Unfinished` counts work that matters: tracked edits (`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`) and unpushed commits (`git rev-list --count HEAD --not --remotes`).
  - `treehouse.Untracked` lists files git doesn't track and `.gitignore` doesn't cover (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z`). Untracked files never block a teardown. They are deleted.
- **TeardownWarned**: a cache flag so the "your tree was kept" comment is posted only once per stay in a status.

## How It Works

```
tick (dispatch.go)
 ├─ treehouse.Status per repo           -> trees (with LeaseHolder)
 ├─ lin.ManagedTickets                   -> tickets
 ├─ leaseHolders(trees, tickets)         -> lin.LeasedTickets(non-managed holders)
 ├─ leaseWorkers -> worker.FindAll       -> Input.Leases[ticket] = []Worker (per tree)
 ├─ inspectTrees                         -> Unfinished / CheckErrors / Untracked per tree
 ├─ reconcile.Plan -> retire() first     -> Teardown | Keep | Stop | Skip
 ├─ settle(cache, ..., heldFinished)     -> drop TeardownWarned once the tree is gone
 └─ execute: teardown() / keep() / stop()
```

**1. Finding the finished tickets** (`retire.go:leaseHolders`)
Collects the distinct `LeaseHolder` values on trees that don't belong to a managed ticket, then calls `linear.Client.LeasedTickets` (`internal/linear/linear.go:283`) for just those identifiers. The query includes archived issues, filters by team, AI label and assignee, and makes no call if nothing qualifies. If the lookup fails, the error is logged and only teardown is skipped for that tick. Launches and nudges still run (`dispatch.go:279-284`).

**2. Mapping trees to workers** (`retire.go:leaseWorkers`, `worker.FindAll`)
Each holder gets one `Worker` per tree it leases. A ticket can hold trees in several repos, and each tree is handled on its own. `WorkspaceID` is set when a herdr workspace is checked out at that path. `State` is `None` when there is no claude agent.

**3. Inspecting git state** (`retire.go:inspectTrees`)
Only looks at holders where `Input.Retires(t)` is true (status is Done and the ticket is not a design ticket). For each tree it runs `treehouse.Unfinished` and `treehouse.Untracked`. Read errors go into `CheckErrors[treePath]`.

**4. Planning** (`internal/reconcile/retire.go`)
`Plan` puts `in.retire()` at the front of the action list (`reconcile.go:186`). For each lease holder in Done or Paused:

- **Labels truncated**: emit `Skip`. The dispatcher can't rule out a design ticket, whose trees belong to the grill and review. Design labels are `design` and `design-review` (`reconcile.go:174`).
- **Design ticket**: ignored entirely.
- **Paused**: emit `Stop` for each tree with a live worker. The tree stays leased.
- **Done**: `retireFinished` handles each tree.
  - Check error or not inspected: `Skip`. The tree stays leased.
  - `Unfinished == ""`: `Teardown`, carrying `RepoDir`, `WorkspaceID`, `TreePath` and `Untracked`. The reason reads "clean and pushed" or "would remove untracked …".
  - Otherwise: `Keep`. All kept trees of the ticket share one comment, attached to the first `Keep`, and only when `TeardownWarned` is not already set. A `Keep` with no live worker and no comment is dropped, so nothing repeats on later ticks.

**5. Executing** (`dispatch.go:429-440`, functions in `retire.go`)
An error in one tree is printed to stderr rather than returned, so other trees still get processed.

- **`teardown`**:
  1. `herdr.CloseWorkspace` runs `herdr workspace close <id>`, if there is a workspace.
  2. `treehouse.Unfinished` runs again, since the worker may have written to the tree between planning and closing. If work turns up, it prints a `Keep` line and returns without commenting. The next tick's plan produces a `Keep` with the comment.
  3. `treehouse.Untracked` runs. If it finds files, `treehouse.RemoveUntracked` runs `git clean -f -d` (ignored files such as build output are left alone), then lists untracked files again. Anything left means `git clean` skipped it, for example a nested git repo. In that case it prints a `Keep` and does not return the tree, since `treehouse return --force` would destroy it.
  4. `treehouse.Return` runs `<treehouse> return <path> --if-lease-holder <ticket> --force` in the repo dir, then prints the action with the reason rewritten to "removed untracked …" so the log names what was actually deleted.
- **`keep`**: closes the workspace if there is one, then posts the comment via `lin.Comment`. `TeardownWarned = true` is set only after Linear accepts the comment, so a failed comment is retried.
- **`stop`**: closes the workspace and nothing else.

**6. Cache bookkeeping** (`dispatch.go:settle`)
`heldFinished` lists Done tickets that still hold a lease. For a ticket that is no longer managed, `settle` keeps `TeardownWarned` only while the ticket still holds a lease. If leases couldn't be read this tick, it keeps the flag regardless (`held == nil`). Once the tree is returned, the flag goes away. A status change also clears it.

## Where Things Live

- `dispatch.go`: the tick. Gathers inputs (around lines 250-333), calls `settle`, dispatches the `Teardown`/`Stop`/`Keep` cases (lines 429-440).
- `retire.go`: side-effecting half: `leaseHolders`, `inspectTrees`, `heldFinished`, `teardown`, `stop`, `keep`, `leaseWorkers`.
- `internal/reconcile/retire.go`: pure planning half: `Input.Retires`, `notDesign`, `retire`, `retireFinished`, `NameList`.
- `internal/reconcile/reconcile.go`: action kinds, `designLabels`, `Plan` ordering.
- `internal/treehouse/treehouse.go`: `Status`, `Return`, `Unfinished`, `Untracked`, `RemoveUntracked`, `gitEnv`.
- `internal/herdr/herdr.go`: `CloseWorkspace`.
- `internal/worker/worker.go`: `FindAll`, `onTree`.
- `internal/linear/linear.go`: `LeasedTickets`.
- `teardown_test.go`: tests for this behaviour.
- `docs/design/decision-log.md` (lines 128, 211, 214, 242): history. Teardown used to be manual, the second Linear query was added for it, and multi-repo leases were handled in ENG-236.

## Gotchas

- **Unpushed means "not on any remote".** A squash-merged branch whose remote copy was pruned counts as unpushed, so the tree is kept and a comment is posted. Probably the most common reason a merged ticket's tree doesn't come back on its own.
- **Only HEAD is checked.** Other local branches in the shared repo don't count, because treehouse returns a tree by detaching HEAD (per the doc comment, treehouse v3.1.2).
- **Untracked files never protect a tree.** They are deleted, with only a log line. Ignored files survive and the tree is returned with them still in it.
- **Nested repos stop the teardown.** The `Keep` path prints a line but posts no comment and doesn't set `TeardownWarned`. The next tick's plan only looks at `Unfinished`, so it plans `Teardown` again and the tree likely cycles through this path every tick. Not traced to a covering test.
- **The tree is checked twice.** Plan-time decides the action; `teardown` re-checks after closing the workspace to catch last-moment worker changes.
- **Not tied to a merged PR.** Any Done-category status triggers it, including Canceled and Duplicate.
- **`--if-lease-holder` guards against races.** If the tree was re-leased between snapshot and return, treehouse refuses and dispatch logs an error.
- **`gitEnv` strips `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` and similar**, so a dispatcher started from a git hook can't point `git clean` at the wrong repo. It also sets `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` to avoid colliding with a worker's git commands.
- **Design tickets and truncated labels are excluded.** Trees of `design`/`design-review` tickets are never retired, and a ticket with more labels than the query reads is skipped every tick.
- **Dry run** prints planned teardowns (including "would remove untracked …") and executes nothing.
- **Not covered**: treehouse's own `return --force` implementation, and the full `teardown_test.go`.

# How dispatch retires the worker and tree of a finished ticket

dispatch never tears down a worker as soon as a ticket is marked done. On each scheduled tick it notices finished tickets that still hold a tree, closes their worker, and returns the tree to the pool, but only if doing so cannot destroy unpushed work.

## Overview

`dispatch run` calls `tick()` in `dispatch.go` once per interval. Each tick reads three sources: the herdr terminal state, the treehouse worktree pools, and Linear. It then calls `reconcile.Plan()`, a pure function, to get a list of actions, and runs them in order. Retirement is one part of that loop. The plan logic is in `internal/reconcile/retire.go` and the side effects are in `retire.go`.

- **Worker** is a whole herdr workspace (the terminal workspace running the worker's Claude), not just a tab. It is retired with `herdr workspace close <id>`.
- **Tree** is a git worktree leased from a treehouse pool. It is retired with `treehouse return <path> --if-lease-holder <ticket> --force`. Just before that, untracked files are deleted with `git clean -f -d`.

## Key Concepts

- **Lease holder**: a tree's `LeaseHolder` field (`treehouse.Tree`) holds the ticket identifier that leased it. Finished tickets are found through their leases, not through a "done" query. A lease whose ticket is not in this tick's managed (started) set must belong to a ticket that is finished or paused.
- **Done / Paused statuses**: set in config as `linear.statuses.done` (default `Done`, `Canceled`, `Duplicate`) and `paused` (default `Backlog`, `Todo`); see `docs/config.md`. A finished ticket loses its worker and its tree. A paused ticket loses only its worker.
- **Unfinished**: `treehouse.Unfinished()` describes what returning a tree would destroy. That means modified or staged tracked files (`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`) or commits on HEAD that no remote has (`git rev-list --count HEAD --not --remotes`). An empty result means it is safe to return.
- **Untracked**: `treehouse.Untracked()` runs `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`. These files never block retirement. They are deleted first, so the log names exactly what was removed.
- **Three action kinds** (in `internal/reconcile/reconcile.go`):
  - `Teardown`: close the workspace and return the tree.
  - `Keep`: close the worker, keep the tree leased, and post one Linear comment.
  - `Stop`: for paused tickets; close the worker and keep the tree.
- **Design tickets are exempt**: tickets labelled `design` or `design-review` own their trees, which belong to the grill and review sessions. A ticket whose labels were cut short (`LabelsTruncated`) is skipped, because dispatch can't rule out that it is a design ticket.

## How It Works

```
tick()  (dispatch.go)
  herdr.Read ─┐
  treehouse.Status (per repo) ─┼─> leaseHolders() ──> lin.LeasedTickets()
  lin.ManagedTickets ─┘               │
                                      v
              leaseWorkers() -> worker.FindAll() per held tree
                                      │
              inspectTrees()  (git reads, only for Retires(t) tickets)
                                      │
              reconcile.Plan() ──> retire() first ──> [Teardown|Keep|Stop|Skip]
                                      │
              settle(cache, held=heldFinished())
                                      │
              execute: teardown() / keep() / stop()   (before any Launch)
```

1. **Discovery.** `tick()` collects every tree from `treehouse.Status()` for each configured repo. `leaseHolders()` (`retire.go`) gathers the lease-holder IDs that are not among the managed tickets and calls `lin.LeasedTickets()`. That query keeps only tickets assigned to the API user and carrying the AI label (or with truncated labels). If the lookup fails, retirement is skipped for this tick, but launches and nudges still run.

2. **Worker mapping.** `leaseWorkers()` calls `worker.FindAll()` (`internal/worker/worker.go`), which returns one `Worker` per tree the ticket holds. A ticket can hold several trees across repos. `onTree()` matches a herdr workspace by `CheckoutPath == tree.Path`. It sets `State` from the workspace's `claude` agent if there is one, and leaves it `None` otherwise.

3. **Inspection.** `inspectTrees()` runs `Unfinished()` and `Untracked()` on each tree of each ticket where `Input.Retires(t)` is true (finished and not a design ticket). It fills three maps: `Unfinished`, `CheckErrors` and `Untracked`. Trees of paused tickets are never inspected, because they are never returned.

4. **Planning.** `Input.retire()` runs first inside `Plan()`. Its actions are placed before parent handling, nudges and launches, so a tree freed by teardown is back in the pool before a launch later in the same tick.
   - Paused ticket: a `Stop` for each tree that has a live worker.
   - Finished ticket: `retireFinished()` decides per tree:
     - A check error, or a tree that was never inspected, gives `Skip`, and the tree stays leased.
     - Empty `Unfinished` gives `Teardown`, carrying the `Untracked` list. The reason reads either "clean and pushed" or "would remove untracked …".
     - Otherwise it gives `Keep`. All kept trees share one comment explaining the reason, attached to the first `Keep`, and only if `Cache[t].TeardownWarned` is false. A `Keep` with no live worker and no comment to post is dropped.

5. **Cache settle.** `settle()` runs before the actions. For tickets that left the managed set, it keeps `TeardownWarned` only while `heldFinished()` says the ticket still holds a lease. Once the tree is returned, the warning flag goes. If the lease lookup failed or a pool was unreadable, `held` is nil and every warning is kept.

6. **Execution** (`retire.go`). Each failure is printed to stderr and does not abort the other trees.
   - `teardown()`:
     1. If there is a `WorkspaceID`, call `herdr.CloseWorkspace()`. Teardown always closes a matched workspace, even one with no live Claude, because an exited Claude leaves its workspace behind.
     2. **Re-check `Unfinished()`** now that the worker is dead. The worker may have written to the tree after the plan was made. If work turns up, it prints a `Keep` line and returns. The tree stays leased, and next tick's plan produces a real `Keep` with a comment.
     3. Re-read `Untracked()`. If there are files, run `RemoveUntracked()` (`git clean -f -d`, which leaves ignored files alone), then list untracked files again. If any survive (git clean skips nested repositories), it prints a `Keep` line and does not return the tree.
     4. Call `treehouse.Return(..., --if-lease-holder <id> --force)`. `--if-lease-holder` stops a tree that was re-leased since the read from being returned under someone else.
   - `keep()`: closes the workspace only if the worker is live. It posts the comment, and sets `TeardownWarned = true` only after Linear accepts it, so a failed post is retried and a successful one never repeats.
   - `stop()`: closes the workspace only.

All git calls use `gitEnv()`. It strips `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` and similar variables, so a dispatcher started from a git hook can't point `git clean` at another repository. It also sets `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` so the reads don't collide with a worker's own git commands.

## Where Things Live

| Concern | Location |
|---|---|
| Tick loop, action execution, `settle()` | `dispatch.go` (`tick`, `settle`) |
| Side effects: `leaseHolders`, `inspectTrees`, `heldFinished`, `teardown`, `keep`, `stop`, `leaseWorkers` | `retire.go` |
| Pure planning: `Retires`, `retire`, `retireFinished`, `NameList` | `internal/reconcile/retire.go` |
| Action kinds, `Input` fields, `designLabels`, `Plan` ordering | `internal/reconcile/reconcile.go` |
| git/treehouse wrappers: `Status`, `Return`, `Unfinished`, `Untracked`, `RemoveUntracked`, `gitEnv` | `internal/treehouse/treehouse.go` |
| `CloseWorkspace` | `internal/herdr/herdr.go` |
| Tree-to-workspace matching | `internal/worker/worker.go` (`FindAll`, `onTree`) |
| `LeasedTickets` query | `internal/linear/linear.go` |
| `TeardownWarned` | `internal/cache/cache.go` |
| Tests | `teardown_test.go` |

## Gotchas

- **Two safety checks, on purpose.** The plan-time check decides what to do. The check in `teardown()` after the workspace is closed protects against a worker writing after the snapshot. A `Keep` from the second check is only printed to stdout; the Linear comment comes on the next tick.
- **Leftovers from a nested repo.** If `git clean` leaves something behind (a nested repository), `teardown()` prints a `Keep` line and returns. As far as I can tell, every later tick plans `Teardown` again and prints the same line. No Linear comment is ever posted on this path, so the tree stays leased until someone removes the nested repo by hand. This was not confirmed against `teardown_test.go`.
- **Ignored files.** `RemoveUntracked` deliberately leaves `.gitignore`d files, but `treehouse return --force` discards anything left. Build output is therefore still dropped at return; it just isn't named in the log.
- **Which workspaces get closed.** `Teardown` closes any workspace whose checkout path matches the tree. `Keep` and `Stop` close one only when a live Claude agent is in it, so a workspace someone opened by hand on a kept tree is left open.
- **Partial failures.** If `CloseWorkspace` fails, nothing else happens and the next tick tries again. If `Return` fails after `git clean`, the untracked files are already gone. The next tick sees a clean tree and retries the return.
- **What "unpushed" means.** Only HEAD's reachability from any remote counts. Other local branches are ignored, since the pool's trees share one repository. A squash-merged branch whose remote copy was pruned counts as unpushed, so it produces a `Keep` and a comment rather than a teardown.
- **Lookup limits.** `LeasedTickets` reads one page. If more than `maxManaged` tickets hold leases, it returns an error and retirement is skipped for the tick. Lease holders that are not assigned to the API user, or lack the AI label, are never retired.
- **Statuses in neither list.** A ticket moved to a status that is in neither `done` nor `paused` keeps its worker running (documented in `docs/config.md`).

# How dispatch retires the worker and tree of a finished ticket

## Overview

Dispatch never retires a worker the moment its ticket finishes. Teardown is part of the regular reconcile **tick** (`tick()` in `dispatch.go`), which `dispatch run` repeats every `interval_minutes`. The trigger is a status change in Linear. When a PR merges, Linear's GitHub integration moves the ticket to a status in `linear.statuses.done` (default `Done`, `Canceled`, `Duplicate`). Dispatch itself never moves a built ticket to Done. On the next tick, dispatch sees that a finished ticket still holds a treehouse lease, and decides one of three things for each tree: tear it down, keep it, or skip it.

The design splits a pure planner from an executor. `reconcile.Plan()` (in `internal/reconcile/`) decides what to do from a snapshot of Linear, herdr and git. `teardown()`, `keep()` and `stop()` (in the root `retire.go`) then run herdr, git and treehouse commands. The main rule is that **a tree is never returned if returning it would destroy work**. Untracked files don't count as work: they are deleted with `git clean`.

## Key Concepts

- **treehouse**: a pool of git worktrees for each repo. A launch *leases* a tree with the ticket identifier as `LeaseHolder`. `treehouse return` gives the tree back to the pool.
- **herdr**: the terminal multiplexer that hosts workers. Each worker runs in a herdr **workspace** whose `CheckoutPath` is the leased tree. The workspace holds the tabs and panes, and the Claude agent runs in one of those panes. Closing the workspace ends the worker process. Dispatch has no separate per-tab or per-process kill.
- **Lease holder**: a ticket that holds a tree but is not among the "managed" (started-status) tickets. Finished and paused tickets are found this way.
- **Unfinished**: a short description of what returning a tree would destroy: modified or staged tracked files, and/or commits reachable from HEAD that no remote has. An empty string means the tree is safe to return.
- **Action kinds** (`internal/reconcile/reconcile.go`):
  - `Teardown` closes the workspace, cleans the tree and returns it.
  - `Keep` closes the workspace (if a worker is live), leaves the tree leased and comments once.
  - `Stop` handles a paused ticket: it closes the workspace and keeps the tree.
  - `Skip` reports why nothing was done.
- **`TeardownWarned`**: a cache flag (`internal/cache/cache.go`) that limits the "your tree has work" comment to one per ticket.

## How It Works

```
tick()                                   dispatch.go
 ├─ herdr.Read()           -> snapshot of workspaces/tabs/agents
 ├─ treehouse.Status()     -> every tree + LeaseHolder, per repo
 ├─ lin.ManagedTickets()   -> started tickets only
 ├─ leaseHolders()         -> lin.LeasedTickets() for leases not in the managed set
 ├─ leaseWorkers()         -> worker.FindAll(): tree -> workspace -> claude agent
 ├─ inspectTrees()         -> treehouse.Unfinished() + treehouse.Untracked() per tree
 ├─ reconcile.Plan()       -> in.retire() first, then parents, watches, launches
 │     └─ retireFinished() -> Teardown | Keep | Skip per tree
 ├─ settle()               -> cache roll-forward (TeardownWarned retention)
 └─ execute actions in order
       Teardown -> teardown()   Keep -> keep()   Stop -> stop()
```

**1. Finding finished tickets that still hold trees.** `lin.ManagedTickets()` returns only started tickets, so a Done ticket drops out of that list. `leaseHolders()` in `retire.go` collects every `tree.LeaseHolder` that is not a managed ticket. It then makes one more Linear call, `LeasedTickets()` in `internal/linear/linear.go`, which looks those tickets up by identifier whatever their status, archived ones included. It makes no call when every lease belongs to a managed ticket. If this lookup fails, the tick logs the error and skips teardown, but launches and nudges still run.

**2. Mapping trees to workers.** `leaseWorkers()` calls `worker.FindAll()` (`internal/worker/worker.go`) for each holder, which gives one `Worker` per leased tree. A ticket can lease trees in several repos, for example when its design includes a library. For each tree, `onTree()` finds the herdr workspace whose `CheckoutPath` equals the tree path, then the `claude` agent in that workspace. The result has a `WorkspaceID` even when Claude has exited; in that case `State` is `None`.

**3. Reading git state before planning.** `inspectTrees()` runs only for holders where `Input.Retires(t)` is true, meaning the status is in Done and the ticket is not a design ticket. For each tree it calls:
- `treehouse.Unfinished()`, which runs `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` and `git rev-list --count HEAD --not --remotes`.
- `treehouse.Untracked()`, which runs `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z`.

Any error goes into `CheckErrors[path]`.

**4. Planning (`internal/reconcile/retire.go`).** `Plan()` puts `in.retire()` first, so a tree returned this tick is free for a launch later in the same tick. `retire()` handles each holder in this order:
- If the ticket is neither done nor paused, it is ignored.
- If `LabelsTruncated` is set, the result is `Skip`. The planner can't tell whether this is a design ticket.
- Design tickets (`design`, `design-review`) are silently left alone, because their trees belong to the grill and review flows.
- A paused ticket gets a `Stop` for each tree with a live worker (`State != None`). The tree stays leased.
- A done ticket goes to `retireFinished()`, which decides each tree independently:
  - If the tree has a check error or was not inspected, the result is `Skip` and the tree stays leased.
  - If `Unfinished` is empty, the result is `Teardown`, carrying `RepoDir`, `WorkspaceID`, `TreePath` and the `Untracked` list. The reason reads "clean and pushed" or "would remove untracked …".
  - If `Unfinished` is not empty, the result is `Keep`. `WorkspaceID` is set only if a worker is live. All of the ticket's kept trees share **one** comment, placed on the first `Keep`, and only if `Cache[id].TeardownWarned` is false. A `Keep` with no live worker and no comment to post is dropped.

**5. Executing (`retire.go`).** In `dispatch.go` the action loop catches and logs errors from each action, so one tree's failure doesn't stop the others.

`teardown()` runs these steps:
1. If `WorkspaceID != ""`, it calls `herdr.CloseWorkspace()`, which runs `herdr workspace close <id>`. This closes every pane and tab and ends the worker. A Teardown always closes the workspace, even if Claude already exited, because an exited worker leaves its workspace behind.
2. It **re-checks** `treehouse.Unfinished()`. The worker could have written to the tree between planning and the close. If work turns up now, it prints a `Keep` line and returns without returning the tree. The next tick's plan then posts the comment.
3. It calls `treehouse.Untracked()` again. If files exist, `treehouse.RemoveUntracked()` runs `git clean -f -d`, which leaves ignored files such as build output alone. It then calls `Untracked()` once more. If anything is left, it prints a `Keep` and stops; see Gotchas.
4. `treehouse.Return()` runs `treehouse return <path> --if-lease-holder <ticket> --force` in the repo dir.
5. It prints the action, whose reason now names the files that were actually removed.

`keep()` closes the workspace if `WorkspaceID` is set. It then posts `a.Text` as a Linear comment and sets `TeardownWarned = true`, but only after Linear accepts the comment, so a failed post is retried on the next tick.

`stop()` only calls `herdr.CloseWorkspace()`.

**6. Cache bookkeeping.** `settle()` in `dispatch.go` runs before the actions:
- A ticket no longer in the managed set keeps `TeardownWarned` only while `heldFinished()` says it still holds a lease. Once the tree is returned, the flag goes away.
- If the lease lookup failed or a repo's pool couldn't be read, `held` is nil and every warning is kept.
- A status change on a managed ticket resets `TeardownWarned`.

## Where Things Live

- `dispatch.go`, `tick()`: gathers inputs, calls `Plan`, runs `settle`, and dispatches actions to the executors.
- `retire.go` (root package): `leaseHolders`, `inspectTrees`, `heldFinished`, `leaseWorkers`, and the executors `teardown`, `keep`, `stop`.
- `internal/reconcile/retire.go`: the pure planning logic (`Retires`, `retire`, `retireFinished`, `NameList`).
- `internal/reconcile/reconcile.go`: `Action`, the `Kind` values, `Input`, `Plan` ordering and `designLabels`.
- `internal/treehouse/treehouse.go`: `Status`, `Return`, `Unfinished`, `Untracked`, `RemoveUntracked`, `gitEnv`.
- `internal/herdr/herdr.go`: `Read` (the snapshot) and `CloseWorkspace`.
- `internal/worker/worker.go`: the tree to workspace to agent lookup.
- `internal/linear/linear.go`: `LeasedTickets`.
- `internal/cache/cache.go`: `TeardownWarned`.
- Tests: `teardown_test.go`. User-facing docs: `docs/guide.md` ("Teardown and pausing") and the `done` row in `docs/config.md`.

## Gotchas

- **Check, close, re-check.** The planning-time git check alone isn't trusted. `teardown()` checks again after the workspace is closed, because the worker could have committed or edited files in between. In that case the worker is already gone but the tree stays leased.
- **Nested repositories survive `git clean`.** `git clean -f -d` skips a nested git repo, and `treehouse return --force` would discard it. So `teardown()` lists untracked files again after cleaning and keeps the tree if anything is left.
- **Untracked files never block teardown.** Only tracked changes and unpushed commits keep a tree. Gitignored files are neither listed nor deleted.
- **A squash-merged branch whose remote branch was deleted counts as unpushed.** HEAD's commits are no longer on any remote, so the tree is kept and the user has to discard the work by hand (`docs/guide.md`). Other local branches don't count, because treehouse returns a tree by detaching HEAD and leaves branches in place.
- **`gitEnv()` strips `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` and similar variables.** A dispatcher started from a git hook would otherwise point git, and the `git clean`, at the wrong repository. It also sets `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` so the checks don't collide with a worker's own git commands.
- **`--if-lease-holder` guards against races.** If the tree was re-leased to another ticket after the snapshot, `Return` leaves it alone.
- **`Keep` and `Stop` close a workspace only if a worker is live; `Teardown` closes it whenever one exists.** This avoids closing a workspace someone opened by hand on a kept tree, but still cleans up workspaces left behind by exited workers.
- **Dry-run (`dispatch tick --dry-run`) still runs the read-only git inspection.** It prints the "would remove untracked …" reasons without acting.
- **Gap:** I did not trace what treehouse does internally on `return --force`. That is an external binary; the code comments say v3.1.2 detaches HEAD.

# How dispatch retires the worker and tree of a finished ticket

## Overview

Retirement is part of the normal tick (`tick` in `dispatch.go`). Dispatch never needs to see a ticket "finish". On every tick it goes from each leased worktree to the Linear ticket that holds it. If that ticket is in a finished status, dispatch closes the herdr workspace, deletes leftover untracked files and returns the tree to the treehouse pool. If the tree still holds tracked work, dispatch keeps the tree and posts one comment.

Like everything else, retirement is split into a side-effect-free planner (`reconcile.Plan` → `Input.retire()` in `internal/reconcile/retire.go`) and an executor (`teardown`, `keep`, `stop` in the top-level `retire.go`). The trigger is a ticket status. Linear's GitHub integration moves a ticket to Done when its PR merges, and dispatch never sets Done on a built ticket itself (`docs/guide.md:38`). "Finished" means any status in `[linear.statuses].done`, which defaults to Done, Canceled and Duplicate (`internal/config/config.go:75`).

The design rule is: never destroy work. A tree goes back to the pool only if it has no modified or staged tracked files and its HEAD is reachable from some remote. Untracked files count as scratch and are deleted. Anything else keeps the tree leased: the worker is stopped and the ticket gets one comment. Git state is checked twice, once while planning and again after the workspace is closed, because the worker could write in between.

## Key Concepts

- **Tree**: a treehouse-leased worktree. `treehouse.Tree.LeaseHolder` is the ticket identifier (`internal/treehouse/treehouse.go:15`). This lease is how dispatch links a ticket to its worktree.
- **Worker**: lease → herdr workspace whose `CheckoutPath` equals the tree path → the `claude` agent in that workspace (`internal/worker/worker.go:55`). `State` is `None`, `Working`, `Idle` or `Blocked`. `FindAll` returns one Worker per tree, because a ticket can lease trees in several repos.
- **Lease holders**: tickets that hold a lease but are not among the managed (started-status) tickets. This is how finished and paused tickets are found.
- **Action kinds** (`internal/reconcile/reconcile.go:32-40`):
  - `Teardown`: close the workspace, clean the tree, return it.
  - `Keep`: close a live worker's workspace, keep the tree leased, maybe post a comment.
  - `Stop`: for a paused ticket, close the worker's workspace and keep the tree.
- **`Unfinished` / `Untracked` / `CheckErrors`**: the git inspection results that Plan reads, keyed by tree path.
- **`cache.Entry.TeardownWarned`**: makes sure the "your tree holds work" comment is posted only once (`internal/cache/cache.go:52`).

## How It Works

```
tick
 ├─ herdr.Read (snapshot)   treehouse.Status per repo (trees + LeaseHolder)
 ├─ lin.ManagedTickets
 ├─ leaseHolders()  → lin.LeasedTickets(ids not in managed)
 ├─ leaseWorkers()  → worker.FindAll per holder
 ├─ inspectTrees()  → Unfinished / Untracked / CheckErrors (only for Retires(t))
 ├─ reconcile.Plan  → retire() first, then parents, watch, launches
 ├─ settle(cache, held=heldFinished)
 └─ execute: Teardown→teardown()  Keep→keep()  Stop→stop()
```

**1. Finding finished tickets.** `tick` reads every repo's pool with `treehouse.Status` (`dispatch.go:258`). `leaseHolders` (`retire.go:20`) collects the lease-holder ids that are not managed tickets. It makes no Linear call if there are none. Otherwise it calls `linear.Client.LeasedTickets` (`internal/linear/linear.go:283`), which fetches those tickets in any status, archived ones included. The query is limited to the configured teams, the API key owner's tickets, and the `ai` label (plus tickets whose labels were truncated). It returns an error rather than reading a partial page. If the lookup fails, the tick logs the error and skips only retirement; launches and nudges still run (`dispatch.go:279-284`). `leaseWorkers` then maps each holder to its `worker.FindAll` results.

**2. Inspecting git state.** `inspectTrees` (`retire.go:38`) runs only for holders where `Input.Retires(t)` is true, meaning the status is in Done and the ticket is known not to be a design ticket (`internal/reconcile/retire.go:17`). For each tree it calls:

- `treehouse.Unfinished`: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` plus `git rev-list --count HEAD --not --remotes`. It returns a human phrase such as "uncommitted changes and 2 commits that no remote has", or "" if the tree is clean.
- `treehouse.Untracked`: `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z`.

Any error goes into `CheckErrors`. All git calls use `gitEnv()`, which strips `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` and similar variables and sets `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` (`treehouse.go:133`).

**3. Planning** (`internal/reconcile/retire.go`). `Plan` puts `in.retire()` first (`reconcile.go:186`), so a tree freed this tick can be leased by a launch later in the same tick. `retire()` goes through the lease holders:

- Not done and not paused: ignored. This includes In Review and Needs Human tickets.
- `LabelsTruncated`: `Skip`. Dispatch can't rule out a design label, so it leaves the tree alone.
- Design or design-review: silently ignored, because the grill and review own those trees.
- Paused (default Backlog, Todo): one `Stop` per tree whose worker is live (`State != None`).
- Done: handled by `retireFinished`, which decides per tree:
  - The tree is in `CheckErrors`, or it was never inspected → `Skip`, and the tree stays leased.
  - `Unfinished == ""` → `Teardown`. The action carries `RepoDir`, `WorkspaceID` and `TreePath`, plus the `Untracked` list for the log message ("would remove untracked a.txt b.txt").
  - Otherwise → `Keep`. `WorkspaceID` is set only if a live agent exists. All kept trees of one ticket share a single comment, attached to the first `Keep`, and only if `!Cache[id].TeardownWarned`. A `Keep` with no live worker and no comment to post is dropped.

**4. Executing.** The executor switch is at `dispatch.go:429-440`. Errors are logged per action and do not stop the loop.

- `teardown()` (`retire.go:77`):
  1. If `WorkspaceID != ""`, call `herdr.CloseWorkspace` (`herdr workspace close <id>`). This kills the Claude session along with its panes and tabs. A failure here aborts, so the tree stays leased.
  2. Re-check `Unfinished`. If work appeared while the workspace was closing, it prints a `keep` line and returns. The next tick plans a `Keep` with the comment.
  3. Re-list untracked files. If there are any, run `treehouse.RemoveUntracked` (`git clean -f -d`, which leaves ignored files alone) and list again. Anything left is usually a nested git repository, which `git clean` skips. In that case it prints a "survived git clean" `keep` line and keeps the tree.
  4. Call `treehouse.Return`, which runs `treehouse return <path> --if-lease-holder <ticket> --force`. The holder pin means a tree re-leased to another ticket since the snapshot is left alone.
  5. Print the action, with the reason rewritten to "removed untracked …".
- `keep()` (`retire.go:129`): closes the live workspace if there is one. It then posts `a.Text` through `lin.Comment` and sets `TeardownWarned = true` only after Linear accepts the comment, so a refused comment is retried next tick.
- `stop()`: closes the workspace and keeps the tree. Moving the ticket back to In Progress relaunches a worker on that kept tree.

**5. Cache bookkeeping** (`settle`, `dispatch.go:534`). Finished tickets are no longer in the managed set, so their cache entries are cut down to the fields that must outlive the ticket's absence. `TeardownWarned` survives only while `heldFinished` (`retire.go:62`) says the ticket still holds a lease, so it is dropped once the tree is returned. If the lease lookup failed or a pool could not be read, `held` is nil and every warning is kept, so a transient failure can't cause a repeat comment. A ticket that comes back into a managed status has `TeardownWarned` reset because its status changed. So if it is reopened and finishes dirty again, it gets a new comment.

**Related escalation: canceled blockers** (`internal/reconcile/parents.go:45,85`). A ticket moved to Canceled or Duplicate is retired like Done. Separately, `planParents` escalates any Todo child whose blocker is `Abandoned` (canceled or duplicate), because that child would otherwise wait forever. A blocker that is merely Done does not count as abandoned. This sits beside teardown rather than inside it.

## Where Things Live

- `dispatch.go`: `tick` wiring (lease lookup, `inspectTrees`, `settle`, the executor switch).
- `retire.go`: the executor side (`leaseHolders`, `inspectTrees`, `heldFinished`, `teardown`, `keep`, `stop`, `leaseWorkers`).
- `internal/reconcile/retire.go`: the pure planner (`Retires`, `retire`, `retireFinished`, `NameList`).
- `internal/reconcile/reconcile.go`: the `Kind`/`Action`/`Input` definitions and the ordering in `Plan`.
- `internal/treehouse/treehouse.go`: the git and treehouse calls (`Unfinished`, `Untracked`, `RemoveUntracked`, `Return`).
- `internal/herdr/herdr.go:130`: `CloseWorkspace`.
- `internal/worker/worker.go`: lease → workspace → agent lookup.
- `internal/cache/cache.go:52`: `TeardownWarned`.
- `teardown_test.go`: about 45 end-to-end scenarios; the test names read as a spec.
- `docs/guide.md` ("Teardown and pausing", around line 108): the user-facing description.

## Gotchas

- **Closing a workspace differs by action.** A `Teardown` always closes the workspace, even when no agent is in it, because a worker whose Claude exited leaves an empty workspace behind. `Keep` and `Stop` close a workspace only if a live agent is in it, so a workspace you opened by hand on a kept or paused tree stays open (`reconcile.go:95-99`).
- **A squash-merged branch whose remote branch was deleted counts as unpushed.** `rev-list HEAD --not --remotes` finds nothing that contains those commits, so the tree is kept and commented on, and a human has to discard it (`docs/guide.md:158`). Unpushed commits on other local branches of the shared repo are deliberately ignored.
- **The dirty-tree comment is posted once.** Pushing later just lets the next tick return the tree; it posts no new comment. The comment only repeats if the ticket is reopened and finishes dirty again.
- **Dry runs plan but don't act.** `tick --dry-run` prints the planned teardowns (with the "would remove untracked" list) but deletes nothing. The re-check after closing the workspace only happens in a real tick.
- **Failures leave the tree leased.** If closing the workspace or `treehouse return` fails, the error goes to stderr and the tree stays leased. Nothing records the failure, so the next tick simply retries.
- **Truncated labels block retirement.** A ticket with more labels than one page reads (`labels(first: 25)`) is never torn down. It produces a `Skip` line every tick until labels are removed.
- **Untracked files can't protect a tree.** Whatever a worker left untracked is gone after teardown, unless `.gitignore` covers it or it is a nested repo.

**Gap:** the treehouse binary itself was not read, so what `return --force` does beyond detaching HEAD (per the `Unfinished` doc comment, "treehouse v3.1.2") is inferred, not verified.

# Why does the breakdown step create each ticket in Backlog and move it to Todo only after linking its blockers?

## The Code in Question
The rule is in the "Still to settle" list in `docs/design/decision-log.md:177`:

> **Ticket creation.** A script creates each ticket in Backlog, links it to its blockers, then moves it to Todo, so no tick promotes it before its blockers are attached. This amends decision 3's single `save_issue` call.

I found no breakdown script in the repo, so this is a design decision that has not been built yet. The dispatcher side it protects is in `docs/design/blueprint.md:218` (reconcile step 7). That step promotes a Todo child of an In Progress parent when "its blockers are all Done".

## What We Found
- **Stated reason.** The decision log says the order exists so that "no tick promotes it before its blockers are attached."
- **What a tick does.** Step 7 of the dispatcher promotes any Todo child of an In Progress parent whose blockers are all Done (`blueprint.md:218`). A Todo child with no blockers attached has no unfinished blockers, so it counts as promotable. Promotion moves the ticket to In Progress, which starts a worker (`blueprint.md:56`, `:256`).
